findings.title: v2 does not carry the society entity overrides, so a society client applying v2 gets the exact two-accounts-one-name defect 0156 S2 exists to discharge
findings.evidence: The seed copies only two child tiers: coa_template_families (0295:249-254) and coa_template_accounts (0295:255-261). clara.coa_template_entity_overrides is keyed BY template_id (0156:401 `primary key (template_id, entity_type, account_code)`) and its two shipped rows are seeded against v1 ONLY (0156:443-459 `where t.scope='platform' and t.template_key='my_sme_starter' and t.version = 1`). MEASURED read-only on clara_l08: `select o.template_id, t.version, o.entity_type, o.account_code, o.override_name, o.suppress from clara.coa_template_entity_overrides o join clara.coa_templates t on t.id=o.template_id` returns exactly two rows, both on v1 (af0d7c77). PROVEN read-only through the estate's own one spelling: `select t.version, a.account_code, a.name, clara._coa_effective_account_name(t.id, a.account_code, a.name, 'society') from clara.coa_template_accounts a join clara.coa_templates t on t.id=a.template_id where t.scope='platform' and a.account_code in ('3040','3900')` returns -- v1: 3040 -> NULL (suppressed), 3900 'Retained Earnings' -> 'Accumulated Fund'; v2: 3040 -> 'Accumulated Fund' (planted), 3900 -> 'Retained Earnings' (NOT relabelled). clara._coa_plant_family reads exactly that helper at 0156:666 and skips only on NULL (0156:669 `continue when v_name is null`), so a society client on v2 is planted BOTH 3040 'Accumulated Fund' AND 3900 'Retained Earnings'. Reachable on the DEFAULT plan: equity_common is `core` and equity_society is `opt_in` with entity_types={society} (measured on both versions), and clara._coa_family_plan keeps a family that declares an axis the client positively matches, so a society client's default plan contains both families. It is silent on every axis: coa_template_drift reads the SAME helper (0156:1144) so the instrument agrees with the mistake; the only society cells in the estate (coa-template-pr-b.test.mjs:905-954) run against `platformStarter()`, which is pinned to version = 1 (coa-template-pr-b-helpers.mjs:198); and coa-template-pr-b.test.mjs:952 asserts the GLOBAL override count is exactly 2, which still holds precisely because 0295 added none. VERIFIED: coa-template-pr-b.test.mjs 43/43 pass on this head. 0295's own tail checks families, accounts, hashes, the special-marker census, code collisions and the freeze triggers (0295:300-441) and never reads the override table.
findings.why: 0156's own M3/M4 mutants (coa-template-pr-b.test.mjs:28-29) name this exact outcome as the defect: 'delete the society/3900 relabel -> the society chart plants Retained Earnings' and 'delete the society/3040 suppression -> the society chart plants 3040 as well'. 0295 produces both outcomes for every society client who adopts v2, without deleting anything, because v2 is a different template_id and the override rows are template-scoped. The pre-step was asked to add four rows; it also silently regressed the society chart. That is beyond the scope asked for and no ruling licenses it.
findings.fix: In 0295 (or a follow-up migration before this wave releases), copy the override rows to v2 with the same INSERT ... SELECT shape the families and accounts use: `insert into clara.coa_template_entity_overrides(template_id, entity_type, account_code, override_name, suppress, basis) select v2_id, o.entity_type, o.account_code, o.override_name, o.suppress, o.basis from clara.coa_template_entity_overrides o where o.template_id = v1_id;` placed AFTER the accounts insert (the FK fk_coa_override_account references coa_template_accounts(template_id, account_code)), plus a tail assertion that v2's override census equals v1's. Add a cell to wave4-chart-rows.test.mjs that drives a SOCIETY client (newInterviewClient with answers {entity_type:'society'}, the shape coa-template-pr-b.test.mjs:906 already uses) through apply_coa_template against the current template and asserts 3900 planted as 'Accumulated Fund' and 3040 absent -- the mirror of coa-template-pr-b.test.mjs:905-921 on v2. Separately, change coa-template-pr-b.test.mjs:952 from a global `count(*) = 2` to a per-template count, so that assertion stops masking this class of omission.

findings.title: The pre-step's acceptance -- a new client gets the four rows through the client-creation door -- is met by the test's own rule, not by the product: the picker lists v1 first with an identical title and no default
findings.evidence: Traced every path. The runtime picks no template at all: interview.v3.questions.ts:38-52 states why clientOnboarding/interview never reach apply_coa_template, clientOnboarding.v4.ts:36 repeats it, and coa-interview-v4.test.mjs:176-187 asserts the absence positively. do-actions.ts names apply_coa_template only in a comment (do-actions.ts:75). OnboardingSettledCard.tsx:135,155 says ApplyStandardChartControl is the ONLY surface for clara.apply_coa_template. That control reads listPublishedCoaTemplates (ApplyStandardChartControl.tsx:72), which filters on state === 'published' and nothing else (apps/web/lib/onboarding/coa.ts:137-149), and renders every row (ApplyStandardChartControl.tsx:261-265). So: NO path preselects the first row, takes [0] or `limit 1`, pins version = 1, or otherwise defaults a new client to v1 -- the select opens on an empty value (ApplyStandardChartControl.tsx:260 `<option value="">{t("templateNone")}</option>`) and confirm is disabled until a row is chosen (:241 `confirmDisabled={!chosen || selected.size === 0}`). The human always picks. But clara.list_coa_templates() orders `by t.scope, t.template_key, t.version` ASCENDING (0150:1286), so v1 renders ABOVE v2, and MEASURED on clara_l08 both rows carry the identical title 'Malaysian SME Standard Chart of Accounts (starter)' and both are state='published'; the only distinction is the version and account count inside the option label (ApplyStandardChartControl.tsx:263, `t("templateOption", { title, version, accounts })`). Nothing marks v2 as current and nothing retires v1.
findings.why: The wave-4 lanes (#941, #942, #946, #949) are built on the premise stated in 0295's own header -- 'every lane consumes the rows BY NAME'. A bookkeeper who picks the first, familiar, identically-titled option gets a 142-account chart with none of 1180/2030/2040/2050, and all four lanes then fail to resolve their accounts for that client. The migration's README section is honest about this ('a NEW client reaches the four rows only by a human picking v2', packages/db/README.md 0295 section), but the implementer's report headlines acceptance point (3) as 'A new client gets the four rows', proved by the TEST's own `order by version desc limit 1` rule, which is dba-coding-lane-classification.test.mjs's convention and not a rule the product implements anywhere.
findings.fix: Resolve the v1 disposition before this wave releases, not after. Cheapest correct option: retire v1 in the same migration (`update clara.coa_templates set state='retired', retired_at=now() where id = v1_id`) so listPublishedCoaTemplates drops it from the picker while every existing adoption and every version=1-pinned test keeps reading the row. That needs an owner ruling, because retiring v1 is a product decision none of the four rulings made. If the owner prefers to keep both visible, the picker must mark the current one and default to it, which is a web change this pre-step does not carry. Either way, file the ticket and name it in the wave's release gate rather than shipping the lanes on a chart a human may not have picked.

findings.title: The redo branch does not tear down coa_template_entity_overrides, so fixing S1 breaks the redo on a foreign key
findings.evidence: The redo deletes exactly three tiers: coa_template_accounts, coa_template_families, coa_templates (0295:199-201). The full set of tables referencing this family, measured from pg_constraint on clara_l08: coa_template_families -> coa_templates, coa_template_accounts -> coa_template_families, coa_template_adoptions -> coa_templates(id, version), coa_template_entity_overrides -> coa_template_accounts(template_id, account_code). Adoptions are refused outright (0295:190-193). Overrides are neither deleted nor refused. Harmless on this head only because v2 carries none (S1).
findings.why: The fix for S1 seeds override rows on v2. The very next redo of 0295 would then hit `delete from clara.coa_template_accounts where template_id = v2_id` with a live fk_coa_override_account child and fail, turning the #957 redo branch from proven-by-construction into broken.
findings.fix: Add `delete from clara.coa_template_entity_overrides where template_id = v2_id;` as the FIRST delete in the redo branch, before the accounts delete, in the same commit as the S1 fix.

findings.title: The report's acceptance point (3) overstates what was proven; the migration's own README does not
findings.evidence: Report line 111: '(3) A new client gets the four rows. S3: a client born the same way, applying the CURRENT published template (`... order by version desc limit 1`, dba-coding-lane-classification.test.mjs's own existing convention for "whichever one is live")'. That convention lives only in tests (dba-coding-lane-classification.test.mjs:354,383,408,449 and wave4-chart-rows.test.mjs:70-77); no product code implements it (see S2). The README section the same commit added is accurate: 'a NEW client reaches the four rows only by a human picking v2 (or a fork of it)'. The report's 'Anything unverified' section (lines 207-213) does raise the two-row picker, but frames it as a UI-rendering question rather than as the reason acceptance point (3) is not what it says.
findings.why: Spec axis: every claim in the report is a claim to verify. The headline claim and the caveat contradict each other, and a reader who stops at the acceptance table concludes the product door is proven when only the database door is.
findings.fix: Restate acceptance point (3) as what S3 actually proves -- 'apply_coa_template against v2 plants all four rows through the real client-birth and apply doors' -- and move the picker question from 'Anything unverified' into an open finding with a ticket, per S2.

findings.title: No web unit or e2e fixture models a two-row template list, so the picker change is untested at every layer above the database
findings.evidence: onboarding-amend-and-chart.test.tsx:249-254 builds a ONE-element TEMPLATES array (template_key 'my_sme_starter', version 1, families 3, accounts 42), and every cell that opens the dialog (:281, :300, :353, :403) therefore exercises a single-option select. apps/web/e2e/agentic-finish-mock.mjs:336-345 returns exactly one row from list_coa_templates, and agentic-finish-walk.spec.ts:282,363 selects by id, so the walk passes without ever rendering two options. No MSW handlers, __fixtures__, snapshots or golden files exist in this repo (searched; none found), so there is nothing else to update.
findings.why: These stay green and are not wrong, but the estate now ships a state -- two published rows with the same title -- that no test above the database has ever rendered. Whatever S2 resolves to, the fixture is the place it gets proven.
findings.fix: When S2 is resolved, extend the TEMPLATES fixture to two rows and add a cell for whatever the decision is (v1 absent after retirement, or v2 marked current).

findings.title: 0150's own S8 tail asserts exactly one coa_templates row, so a redo of 0150 on a chain that already has 0295 fails
findings.evidence: 0150:1900 `select id into v_tmpl from clara.coa_templates where scope = 'platform' and template_key = 'my_sme_starter'` -- the only key lookup in the estate with no version filter -- followed by 0150:1903-1906 `select count(*) into v_n from clara.coa_templates; if v_n <> 1 then raise exception 'S8: expected exactly 1 coa_templates row after seeding, found %'`.
findings.why: Order-protected in a normal ladder (0150 runs long before 0295) and already unreachable on any rig, whose firm-scope test templates break the same count. Recorded so nobody discovers it during a redo and blames 0295.
findings.fix: Optional and out of this pre-step's scope: pin 0150:1900 with `and version = 1` and scope its count to `where scope='platform' and template_key='my_sme_starter' and version=1` if a 0150 redo is ever wanted.

answers.q1: No path in the product defaults a new client to v1, and no path defaults it to v2 either -- the human always picks, and the list shows both. Evidence: OnboardingSettledCard.tsx:135,155 states ApplyStandardChartControl is the only surface for clara.apply_coa_template; that control loads listPublishedCoaTemplates (ApplyStandardChartControl.tsx:72), which filters on state === 'published' and nothing else (apps/web/lib/onboarding/coa.ts:137-149), renders every row (:261-265), opens on an empty option (:260) and disables confirm until one is chosen (:241); ApplyStandardChartControl.tsx:225 finds the chosen row by template_id, never by template_key. The runtime picks nothing: interview.v3.questions.ts:38-52 and clientOnboarding.v4.ts:36 forbid it and coa-interview-v4.test.mjs:176-187 asserts the absence. do-actions.ts:75 mentions apply_coa_template only in prose. So the blocker shape the brief named (a preselected first row, a template_key + limit 1, a pinned version = 1) does not exist. What does exist: clara.list_coa_templates() orders by scope, template_key, version ASCENDING (0150:1286), so the 142-account v1 renders ABOVE the 146-account v2; measured on clara_l08 both rows are state='published' and carry the identical title 'Malaysian SME Standard Chart of Accounts (starter)', distinguished only by the version and account numerals inside the option label (:263). I judge that NOT an acceptable outcome to release: the whole premise of this pre-step, stated in 0295's own header, is that the four wave-4 lanes consume these rows BY NAME, and a bookkeeper who picks the first identically-titled option gets a client whose chart has none of them, which breaks all four lanes for that client with no refusal naming why. Recommendation: retire v1 in the same migration (`update clara.coa_templates set state='retired', retired_at=now()` -- listPublishedCoaTemplates then drops it while existing adoptions and every version=1-pinned test keep reading the row), or, if the owner prefers both visible, mark and default to the current one in the picker. Retiring v1 is a product decision no ruling made, so it needs the owner; either way it must be decided before the wave's lanes release, not after. Recorded as S2 (major).
answers.q2: One consumer is pinned to v1 and BREAKS silently: clara.coa_template_entity_overrides, whose two society rows are seeded `where ... version = 1` (0156:443-459) and keyed by template_id (0156:401). See S1 (blocker) -- a society client on v2 is planted both 3040 'Accumulated Fund' and an un-relabelled 3900 'Retained Earnings', proven read-only through clara._coa_effective_account_name. Everything else survives: coa-template-pr-a-helpers.mjs:184-193 (platformTemplate(), pinned to version = 1 by this very diff) and coa-template-pr-b-helpers.mjs:198 (platformStarter(), already pinned) keep every 42/142 assertion deterministic -- VERIFIED by running both batteries on this head, 53/53 and 43/43 pass. dba-coding-lane-classification.test.mjs:354,383,408,449 already read `order by version desc limit 1` so its four cells now silently exercise v2; they assert only count(*) = 0 / > 0 on coa_accounts and stay green -- VERIFIED 15/15 pass. No census or parity check counts platform templates: the only parts-parity file is packages/runtime/scripts/parts-parity-exemptions.mjs with no coa_template reference; rig-meta.mjs:1503-1620 and x42-s5-helpers.mjs:930,957,1510 roster function names and signatures only, and 0295 mints no function; operation-census.test.mjs is unaffected for the same reason. The only content_sha256 literal anywhere is 0295's own v1 pin (0295:117-118). No snapshots, golden files, __fixtures__ or MSW handlers exist in this repo. onboarding_plan items carry no template id (interview.v3.questions.ts:77-99 answers {chart, applied} only), 0218_firm_setup.sql has no chart reference, and the seeds carry no coa_template rows. Web fixtures still model a one-row list -- S5 (nit). 0150:1900-1906 would break on a 0150 redo after 0295 -- S6 (nit).
answers.q3: Confirmed, measured read-only on clara_l08. The migration calls the same helper, never a hand-rolled hash: 0295:281 `v_sha := clara._coa_template_content_sha256(v2_id);` then publishes with it at 0295:282-284, exactly as 0150:1649-1652 published v1. Recomputation matches for both rows: `select t.version, encode(t.content_sha256,'hex'), encode(clara._coa_template_content_sha256(t.id),'hex'), t.content_sha256 = clara._coa_template_content_sha256(t.id)` returns match = t for v1 (d02a786a685d484989a85e2e6a3f239ccdb5cbb8957143ede21f2fd8b12f67df) and v2 (6a36ad00be8c20c231740f89f4308729b0b540c1c2ca8fe2878c979696b7b4ef). The tail re-proves both (0295:315-318 for v1, 0295:338-341 for v2). v1 is unchanged: its hash equals the pinned literal, and its counts are 42 families / 142 accounts, measured directly. v2 is 42 / 146. The migration issues no UPDATE, DELETE or INSERT against v1's own rows anywhere -- read the whole file; the only writes naming v1_id are SELECTs and the `forked_from` value.
answers.q4: All three pins are MEASURED and correct on clara_l08, and all three are the right functions to pin. Measured: `select p.oid::regprocedure::text, encode(sha256(convert_to(p.prosrc,'UTF8')),'hex') from pg_proc p where p.oid in (...)` returns clara._coa_template_content_sha256(uuid) = d120669e12506c1a347729008e3f11785d62c914c3955f3dd6a099fd9b20baa7, clara._tf_coa_template_freeze() = 0fced8e2c635e5bdb306b6836b208cbae44a669f6f6549e3113017c8441d1844, clara._tf_coa_template_child_freeze() = 504d9c613739d30c21c100d3c8c8b8dbc525ff2adeda888d554bbec0309f0ec5 -- byte-identical to 0295:111-116. Right functions: the hash helper is CALLED at 0295:281; both freeze triggers are RELIED UPON (the child freeze is what forces the new-version design at all, and both are disabled and re-armed by the redo branch at 0295:194-202). None of the three is recut by this file. The v1 content_sha256 literal (0295:117-118) is a fourth pin, also measured, asserted in both the prestate (0295:137-140) and the tail (0295:311-314). This is the house's 'pin a function you call but do not recut' convention applied correctly.
answers.q5: Read at 0295:185-203. It tears down coa_template_accounts, coa_template_families and the coa_templates row for v2 (0295:199-201), disables all three freeze triggers immediately before (0295:194-196) and re-enables them immediately after (0295:202-... ) inside the SAME DO block and therefore the same transaction -- precedent 0227:346-348, as cited. It refuses outright if v2 already carries a client adoption (0295:190-193). Triggers are left armed: measured tgenabled = 'O' for all three on clara_l08, and the tail asserts exactly that string at 0295:414-424, independent of which branch ran. A second apply after a redo WOULD produce a byte-identical v2 in every respect the estate reads: forked_from is re-derived as v1's id (same value), the content columns are a verbatim copy plus four literal rows, and clara._coa_template_content_sha256 hashes only the families' and accounts' content -- read its prosrc: it builds jsonb from family_key/label/inclusion/basis/sort_ordinal/msic_*/trade_natures/entity_types and account_code/name/account_type/account_class/special_acc_type/family_key/sort_ordinal/tax_sensitive/add_back_class/statutory, and nothing else -- so no id or timestamp enters the hash. Only the surrogate uuid and created_at/published_at differ, and nothing pins those. ONE gap: the redo does NOT delete coa_template_entity_overrides rows for v2. Harmless on this head because none exist, but it becomes a real break the moment S1 is fixed -- the FK fk_coa_override_account references coa_template_accounts(template_id, account_code), so the accounts delete would fail. Recorded as S3 (minor). The redo was not driven end to end this round, which the report states honestly; I did not drive it either (the brief forbids migrating).
answers.q6: No sentence of the four rulings is contradicted by the placements or the codes, and no ruling asks for a class, tag or marker the rows lack. 1180 Accrued Income in trade_receivables at ordinal 45: #942's ruling says accrued income 'is a current asset presented apart from invoiced trade receivables, so a dedicated row is the ordinary treatment'. The family is labelled 'Trade and Other Receivables' (measured), not 'Trade Receivables', and it already carries 1120 Deposits Paid and 1130 Prepayments -- neither an invoiced trade receivable. Presentation apart from invoiced receivables is carried by the dedicated code, distinct from 1100 Trade Receivables Control; a chart family is a grouping, not a statement line. 2040/2050 in trade_payables: #949's ruling requires 'A NEW dedicated standard-chart liability row, Rent Payable, not 2010 Other Payables and not 2020 Accruals' -- satisfied, 2050 is its own code and the measured v2 family reads 2000 Control / 2010 Other Payables / 2020 Accruals / 2030 Deferred Revenue / 2040 Salaries Payable / 2050 Rent Payable at ordinals 10/20/30/40/50/60. The codes 2040 and 2050 are the implementer's choice, licensed by the ruling naming only the row's name, and the prestate measures the 2031-2099 band empty on v1 before choosing inside it (0295:143-150). No ruling asks for a control-account class: #946 says salaries payable is 'an ordinary liability with no class' and 'deliberately not a control account'; #942 says the asset must be 'active, asset, not a control account'. All four carry account_class null, special_acc_type null, tax_sensitive false, add_back_class null, statutory null (0295:265-274, asserted in the tail at 0295:357-376 and by S1 of the battery). No ruling asks for a statutory tag or an add-back class, and none is added. One ruling instruction is met only in spirit: #941 AC5 and #946 AC1 say 'appends ... to the standard chart template' and 'the template count cells are updated'. 0295 mints a new version instead (because a published template's rows are frozen -- CLR08, 0150:604-663) and pins the count cells to v1 rather than updating them. That is the correct engineering answer to an AC written on a false premise, and it is argued in full in both the migration header and the README. But it is the thing that turns the 'existing clients are not touched' half of those ACs into 'new clients are not reached either' -- see S2.
answers.q7: Correct. packages/db/tests/wave4-chart-rows-preintegration-gate.mjs is registered in packages/db/package.json's `test` script as the LAST `--import`, immediately after 0293's token `--import ./tests/fa-arrears-judgement-scope-preintegration-gate.mjs` and before the `"tests/**/*.test.mjs"` glob -- verified by reading the diff hunk; that one token is the only change to the file. Shape matches the sibling exactly: both are twelve lines, both open with the same 'NOT a test file / preload it for an estate sweep' paragraph, both name the file they mirror, both state the focused-run contract, and both end with a single `process.env.CLARA_ALLOW_MISSING_<NAME> = "1"`. The variable is read in exactly one place (wave4-chart-rows.test.mjs:79), the same one-gate-one-reader shape as CLARA_ALLOW_MISSING_FA_ARREARS_JUDGEMENT_SCOPE (fa-arrears-resolution-fixtures.mjs:92). The focused-run contract holds: the premise block throws loudly when the variable is unset (wave4-chart-rows.test.mjs:78-86).
answers.q8: Everything in the report that I could check, I checked, and all of the numeric and behavioural claims hold. VERIFIED BY RE-RUNNING on clara_l08 at this head: wave4-chart-rows.test.mjs 4 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip (focused, full gate chain, no gate preloaded); coa-template-pr-a.test.mjs 53/53; coa-template-pr-b.test.mjs 43/43; dba-coding-lane-classification.test.mjs 15/15. VERIFIED BY QUERY: every prestate pin, v1's and v2's hashes and counts, the freeze triggers' armed state, the four rows' every flag column, the two family rosters, and the list_coa_templates ordering. VERIFIED BY GREP: the report's own 'no re-sync door' claim -- `grep -rniE 'publish.*existing client|sync.*coa_accounts.*template|backfill.*coa_accounts'` over packages/db/migrations, packages/runtime/workflows, apps/web/lib and apps/web/components returns nothing, so the copy-not-reference argument for existing clients stands. NOT VERIFIED, and I did not attempt them because the brief forbids the acts: the CLARA_MIGRATION_REDO run (the report states plainly it was not driven); the first-apply migrate output (the report quotes it, and the database's end state is consistent with it); `pnpm typecheck` and `CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pnpm lint`; operation-census.test.mjs and rig-isolation.test.mjs. CONTRADICTED: nothing in the report is false, but acceptance point (3) is materially overstated -- see S4 -- and the report's 'Anything unverified' section treats the two-published-versions picker as a cosmetic UI question when it is the reason the product acceptance is unmet (S2). The report does not mention clara.coa_template_entity_overrides anywhere, which is the blocker (S1).

notes: Reviewed read-only. I ran the four test files named above against clara_l08 (their cells roll back) and issued read-only SQL; I ran no migrate, reset, drop or write. The diff's craft is high -- the new-version design is correctly reasoned from a measured refusal, the prestate pins are real, the tail re-reads the catalog rather than trusting the seed, and every cell carries a driven vacuity control. Two things stop it. S1 is a silent accounting regression for society clients that no test in the estate would catch, because the one battery that exercises society charts is pinned to v1 and the one assertion that would have caught it (a global override count of 2) is satisfied precisely by the omission. S2 is the product half of the acceptance: the four rows are reachable but not delivered, and the wave's four lanes are built on the assumption that they are there. S1 is fixable inside this migration in a few lines plus one cell. S2 needs an owner ruling on retiring v1, which no existing ruling covers, and should be settled before the wave's lanes release rather than after.
